articles.title: Home Assistant controls computer speakers and microphones
articles.dek: System Bridge adds audio output selection, volume and mute controls, alongside richer playback controls.
body: Home Assistant adds controls for a computer’s audio devices through System Bridge. The system’s default output gains volume and mute controls and a choice of output, while each output has its own controls. Microphone inputs gain volume and mute settings, with a separate selector for the default input.

The existing media player also gains seeking and volume where the computer reports support. Its source list selects which player to follow, and commands go to that player; this selection resets after a restart. Shuffle and repeat control work on Linux, while Windows can report those settings but cannot change them.

Audio-device support requires System Bridge 5.16.0 or later. Newly connected devices appear as they are discovered, and disconnected ones become unavailable. Per-application volume is outside this addition.

pullRequests.title: Make the System Bridge media player full, with audio devices

articles.title: ESPectre adds live controls for Wi-Fi motion sensing
articles.dek: Sensitivity, detection settings and an on/off switch join ESPHome’s built-in Wi-Fi motion detector.
body: ESPHome adds live controls for its ESPectre Wi-Fi motion detector. Makers can adjust sensitivity and the number of detections needed to turn motion on or off, change the detection algorithm, and pause sensing through a switch instead of rebuilding firmware for each adjustment.

Francesco Pace brings controls previously offered by the external ESPectre component into the built-in integration. New diagnostic sensors also report how consistently Wi-Fi measurements arrive, helping distinguish a quiet room from poor measurement traffic.
The original limit still applies: Wi-Fi motion sensing cannot reliably establish whether a person who remains still is present.

pullRequests.title: [espectre] Update to SDK 3.1.0; add runtime config entities and CSI diagnostics
[espectre] Document SDK 3.1.0 options, runtime controls and diagnostics
[espectre] Add Wi-Fi CSI motion detection component

articles.title: ESPHome displays progressive JPEG photos
articles.dek: Images such as Immich previews no longer fail because of their JPEG format.
body: ESPHome’s online image component accepts progressive JPEGs, including the format commonly served by Immich previews. It previously rejected these files outright, leaving makers unable to display them without converting the image first.
Remco van Essen adds decoding across the existing image sizes and pixel formats. A progressive picture is drawn after its final scan arrives, rather than appearing in successive passes.

These images need extra memory. ESP32 devices use external RAM first, and showing a large image at a smaller size reduces the requirement. If the full decoding buffer does not fit, the component falls back to a blockier image.

pullRequests.title: [runtime_image] Decode progressive and SOF1 JPEGs with JPEGDEC

articles.title: Home Assistant stops OpenRouter actions running twice
articles.dek: A November beta correction prevents duplicate shopping-list additions and restores tool use with affected models.
body: Home Assistant corrects a November beta problem that made OpenRouter conversation agents perform each requested action twice. Asking to add milk to a shopping list could add two entries, while toggling a device could immediately undo the first toggle.

The integration now passes each action on only once when it reads the streamed response. This also avoids duplicate action identifiers that caused Anthropic and Upstage to reject the next request, preventing Claude models from using tools.

articles.title: UniFi Protect detectors report alarms and maintenance events
articles.dek: Smoke-capable sensors gain event entities for alarms, self-tests and device problems.
body: Home Assistant adds alarm and maintenance event entities for UniFi Protect sensors that report smoke-detector support. Smoke and carbon-monoxide alarm events sit alongside self-tests, low battery, cleaning requests, faults and end-of-life notices.

These are events, rather than a continuously active smoke or carbon-monoxide state: the public interface does not supply that state. The change uses the detector’s advertised capabilities, including USL Smoke and UP Sense devices that expose the smoke flag.

pullRequests.title: Add UniFi Protect smoke detector event entities

articles.title: Music Assistant recovers when a group’s lead speaker disappears
articles.dek: Playback resumes on a remaining speaker instead of staying silently stuck on playing.
body: A Music Assistant speaker group resumes playback on a remaining speaker when the speaker leading it drops off the network. Previously, trying to stop the unreachable leader could fail and abort the handover, leaving the group showing that it was playing while the music stayed silent.

Marcel van der Veldt makes the group rebuild even when stopping or disconnecting its former leader fails. This extends earlier work on deliberately powering off a group leader to a speaker that cannot be reached at all. A related Sonos recovery path still needs verification on physical speakers.

pullRequests.title: Fix a speaker group staying silent after its leader drops offline

articles.title: Google Weather gives Home Assistant a closer rain forecast
articles.dek: An on-demand action returns precipitation predictions in two- or fifteen-minute steps.
body: Home Assistant’s Google Weather integration adds an action for retrieving the provider’s detailed precipitation forecast. Depending on the location, the forecast extends up to six hours in two- or fifteen-minute intervals, giving automations more detail about approaching rain. It uses Google’s experimental minute-forecast service.

The action requests fresh data only when called and counts toward the Google Weather API quota. It does not add background polling or a ready-made weather-card display; the data is returned for an automation or other consumer to use.

pullRequests.title: Add get_minute_forecast service to Google Weather

articles.title: ESPHome translations no longer wait for code changes
articles.dek: Finished Device Builder translations can trigger their own release, with translators credited in the notes.
body: Completed ESPHome Device Builder translations can trigger a release even when there are too few code changes to do so. Previously, people could finish translating a language while the installed interface continued using the older snapshot until another release was warranted.
Jesse Hills adds a check against the translations in the previous release. The release notes also thank translators and list the languages that changed, including their completeness.

pullRequests.title: Release on translation changes and credit translators

articles.title: Delayed voice commands keep their original AI agent
articles.dek: Timer-based requests return to the conversation agent that understood them.
body: Home Assistant keeps a delayed command with the AI conversation agent that started it. Previously, a command scheduled through an AI agent’s timer was checked and later run by the built-in agent instead, which could reject a free-form request the AI agent understood.
Passing the original agent through to the timer’s intent handling keeps that request with the same interpreter when its time arrives.

pullRequests.title: Pass the conversation agent to intents called as LLM tools

articles.title: Bluetooth proxies recover stranded devices without a restart
articles.dek: A replacement controller connection releases devices left attached to a stalled session.
body: ESPHome Bluetooth proxies release devices left attached to a stalled controller session when a new connection replaces it. A peripheral that announces itself only while idle can otherwise remain undiscoverable until the proxy restarts.

J. Nick Koston tested the failure with an ESP32 proxy and a peripheral that stops advertising while connected. Replacing the frozen client releases the link, allowing the new client to reconnect. Re-subscribing from the same client keeps its existing links.

pullRequests.title: [bluetooth_proxy] Release held connections when a new client replaces the subscriber

articles.title: Music Assistant’s desktop player recovers after an audio device disconnects
articles.dek: The companion player reopens failed audio connections instead of keeping a dead output.
body: Music Assistant’s desktop player recovers failed audio outputs instead of keeping an unusable connection. On Windows, the system-default setting resolves to the actual audio device, helping playback recover after an output disconnects and returns.

David Bishop also keeps the player registered while no output is available and adds a retry path for Linux audio-service connections. Saved device identifiers keep the selected output tied to the same device when the list of audio devices changes.

pullRequests.title: fix: recover failed audio outputs and use stable device selections

articles.title: Music Assistant accepts more than one Pocket Casts account
articles.dek: Household members can connect their own podcast accounts to the same server.
body: Music Assistant allows multiple Pocket Casts accounts on one server. OzGav enables separate provider instances, each with its own login and account-specific cache. When two accounts subscribe to the same podcast, Music Assistant keeps one library entry linked to both accounts.

articles.title: PIP Solar stops reporting missing readings as inverter faults
articles.dek: Failed polls become unknown states instead of invented numbers and a false fault indication.
body: ESPHome’s PIP Solar integration stops turning a failed or timed-out inverter poll into a fault indication. Missing or unreadable fault codes become unknown, rather than switching the fault sensor on.

The same correction applies to five numeric fields, including output-source priority and solar power-balance settings. Missing values previously became misleading numbers, which varied with the processor. Valid fault codes and readings keep their existing meaning.

pullRequests.title: [pipsolar] Publish an unknown state instead of a bogus value for missing fields

articles.title: CalDAV task edits appear without a fifteen-minute wait
articles.dek: Quick successive check-offs trigger another refresh instead of leaving the old task state on screen.
body: Home Assistant refreshes a CalDAV to-do list again when a task changes while the list is already being read. Previously, the follow-up refresh was skipped, leaving an added, edited or completed task looking unchanged for up to fifteen minutes.

The correction covers quick successive check-offs as well as changes made during a scheduled refresh. Tests with deliberately slowed reads on Nextcloud, Baikal and Radicale confirmed that the extra refresh shows the changes after the ongoing read finishes.

pullRequests.title: Refresh CalDAV to-do lists after a write during an update
